html:
SMTO-SCH-0009 — This prompt can't be scheduled as written

GUID: 26885bce-fad9-496e-8229-e9e0dec0be0e
Slug: schedule-prompt-unsupported
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • SMTO can schedule ordinary requests, but this prompt is empty, too long, starts with a / command, or asks SMTO to type in or use a saved private value. The schedule wasn't saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the prompt starts with /, such as /restart, run that command yourself when you need it instead of scheduling it. Commands that start with / control SMTO itself and can't be scheduled as work for the Agent.
  2. Remove any part that types in a value or uses a saved password, for example typein "..." or "use the sudo password from key ...". Private values like passwords are never stored inside a schedule, so SMTO refuses to save them.
  3. Make sure the prompt isn't empty and isn't extremely long; shorten it to the essential instructions if needed. Scheduled prompts must be between 1 and 24,000 characters.
  4. Schedule the cleaned-up prompt again, using Schedule this prompt or New schedule on the Schedules page. A plain request can run later on its own without needing anything private from you.

What success looks like

  • The schedule saves and the prompt appears on the Schedules page.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste a password or secret into the prompt as a workaround.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Scheduled prompt validation rejected the text: empty or longer than 24,000 characters, starting with an application slash command, or containing private macro syntax (typein, Parameter Store or sudo-password references) that would attach temporary private context.

What this means

  • Scheduled prompt validation rejects empty/over-24,000-character text, a leading application slash command or parsed private macro content. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • Scheduled prompt validation rejects empty/over-24,000-character text, a leading application slash command or parsed private macro content.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect prompt length and command/macro routing while preserving the intended deferred instruction.

How to fix it

  • Schedule a plain Agent prompt of 1 to 24,000 characters (events/prompts.py validate_prompt). Run slash commands such as /restart directly instead of scheduling them, and remove typein or Parameter Store/sudo references, which parse_user_macros treats as private macro context that scheduled prompts cannot carry.
  • Use a bounded ordinary Agent prompt without private macros or temporary context; use immediate command controls for application commands.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported bounded scheduled prompt captures the intended work without transient private macros.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
